title: Frequently sampled Insulin glucose tolerance test
author: Timothy Nichols
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8e8hthw

steps.title: Fast and monitor diet
steps.instruction: Maintain pigs on an overnight fast; monitor food intake for the three days preceding the fast to confirm adequate carbohydrate consumption.

steps.title: Place intravenous catheters
steps.instruction: Insert two intravenous catheters in each pig: one dedicated to blood sampling and the other for infusion of glucose and insulin.

steps.title: Administer glucose bolus
steps.instruction: Deliver a glucose bolus of 0.3 g kg⁻¹ as a 50 % (w/v) solution over approximately 5 minutes.

steps.title: Collect pre‑ and post‑glucose samples
steps.instruction: Draw blood at the following time points relative to the glucose bolus: –15, –10, –5, –1, 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 19 minutes.

steps.title: Administer insulin bolus
steps.instruction: At 20 minutes after the glucose bolus, inject insulin at 0.03 U kg⁻¹.

steps.title: Continue blood sampling
steps.instruction: Continue collecting blood samples at appropriate intervals up to the 180‑minute time point for insulin and glucose measurement.

steps.title: Measure insulin and glucose
steps.instruction: Determine insulin concentrations by radioimmunoassay (RIA, ICN) and glucose concentrations using a YSI analyzer (Yellow Springs, Ohio).

steps.title: Analyze data with MINMOD
steps.instruction: Analyze the glucose and insulin data using the Bergman minimal model (MINMOD Millennium version 6.02) to calculate the insulin sensitivity index (S_I).
